facts.text: Rainey Street was first developed in 1884 by cattle baron Jesse Driskill and Frank Rainey, subdividing 16 acres between the Colorado River and Water Street.
In 1985, amid fears of high‑density redevelopment, the neighborhood was added to the National Register of Historic Places.
Many historic bungalows on Rainey have been renovated into bars and restaurants, each featuring large porches and outdoor yards for patrons.
The construction of Interstate 35 left Rainey Street isolated from the rest of Austin, and by 1978 more than half of its buildings were dilapidated.
Rainey Street now hosts some of Austin’s most vibrant patios and cocktail programs, with live music lighting up the street after sunset.
The Tejano Walking Trail, a nearly 5‑mile loop, passes through Rainey Street, showcasing a broad slice of American history.
